text.p: Some 1.3 million Venezuelan public servants extended their strike into a third day on Thursday, refusing to return to work unless the government fulfilled its promises to pay bonuses, union officials said.
The strike, billed as a 48-hour stoppage when it started on Tuesday, was the most serious labour conflict since President Rafael Caldera took office in February 1994.
"We'll keep up the stoppage until next week if need be ... there is no indication the government has the money to pay," Antonio Suarez, head of the Public Sector Workers Federation said.

Suarez said the government owed staff, who earn an average monthly wage equivalent to $106, a total of 100 billion bolivars ($212 million) in bonuses promised in February. "All we're asking is that they pay what we are owned," he said.

Government officials said some Ministries had already made payments -- although covering the full debt would require further congressional approval. Congress passed a 30 billion bolivar spending request on Tuesday.
Inflation of more than 100 percent over the past twelve months has eroded Venezuelan living standards. The cost of living for a family of five is estimated at 116,000 bolivars ($240).
